title: Crestline Credit Card Statement Rule: Billing Cycle, Due Date, Interest and Printed Minimum
content:
**Statement rule — Crestline Credit Card.** Each billing cycle closes on the cardholder's statement closing day and produces one statement. The payment due date is the statement date plus the product's grace period days.

## Standard interest

Standard interest is charged at the purchase APR on the average daily standard balance, using a daily periodic rate equal to the purchase APR divided by the product's daily rate basis in days. No interest is charged on standard purchases when the previous statement's new balance was paid in full by its due date. When any interest is due in a cycle, it is at least the product's minimum interest charge.

- **Deferred-interest balances** are not charged interest during the plan; their interest is recorded as an accrual each cycle under the deferred-interest rule.
- **Equal-payment balances** carry interest at the plan's equal-payment APR, which is already inside the fixed monthly payment.

| Previous statement's new balance paid in full by its due date | Interest on standard purchases this cycle |
|---|---|
| yes | none |
| no | charged at the daily periodic rate on the average daily standard balance, at least the minimum interest charge |

Hypothetical figures: an average daily standard balance of 1,000 USD over a 30-day cycle at a 24.99% APR and a 365-day basis gives 1,000 multiplied by 24.99 percent divided by 365, multiplied by 30, about 20.54 USD.

## Minimum payment clause — no longer in force

The statement rule formerly stated that the minimum payment is the larger of the payment floor and the product's percentage of the new balance excluding equal-payment plan balances, rounded up to the whole dollar, plus every amount the product adds on top of it (the fixed monthly payment of each equal-payment plan, any past-due amount and a late fee posted in the cycle); that when the new balance is below the payment floor the minimum is the whole new balance; and that while a billing-error dispute is open the disputed amount is left out when the product so provides. **That clause is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis for the minimum payment.** The product figures it names — the payment floor, the percentage of the new balance, the whole-dollar rounding and the amounts added — remain the product's figures.

superseded_clauses: The minimum payment is the larger of min_payment_floor and min_payment_pct_of_balance percent of the new balance excluding equal-payment plan balances, rounded up to the whole dollar (min_payment_rounding), plus every amount listed in min_payment_includes (the fixed monthly payment of each equal-payment plan, any past-due amount and a late fee posted in the cycle); when the new balance is below min_payment_floor the minimum is the whole new balance; while a billing-error dispute is open the disputed amount is left out when disputed_amount_excluded_from_min is true.
